title: You Don’t Need 15 Tools (Just These for Stirred Drinks)
subtitle: Skip the clutter and use what actually makes a difference.
summary:
Most home bars get overcomplicated fast. Drawers full of tools, half of them barely used.

The truth is, for stirred cocktails, you only need a small set of things that actually work. Once you have those dialed in, everything else is just noise.

sections.title: Start With a Proper Mixing Glass
sections.body:
You don’t need anything fancy, but you do need something that gives you control. A solid mixing glass holds temperature better and makes stirring smoother.

This is one of those tools you’ll use constantly, so it’s worth getting right.

sections.title: A Bar Spoon That Actually Feels Good
sections.body:
A good bar spoon makes stirring easier and more consistent. You want something that moves smoothly without fighting you.

If it feels awkward, you’ll notice it immediately.

sections.title: Straining Cleanly Matters
sections.body:
A Hawthorne strainer will handle most drinks. Add a fine mesh strainer if you want a cleaner finish.

This is less about equipment and more about the result — a smoother, more polished drink.

sections.title: Ice Is Part of Your Toolset
sections.body:
Your ice is doing more work than most of your tools. Large cubes for serving, solid ice for stirring — this matters more than adding another gadget.

If you ignore this, everything else suffers.

sections.title: What You Don’t Need
sections.body:
You don’t need a drawer full of specialized tools to make great drinks. Most of them don’t get used.

Start simple, use what works, and add things only when you actually need them.
